figures.name: a cat sitting, seen from the side, tail raised
figures.how: I made the body a tall wedge (both large triangles plus the medium one), put a diamond head with two small-triangle ears on top, and used the parallelogram as a tail; looking at the silhouette I turned the tail from a flat one along the ground into one rising up from the back.
figures.seen_before: yes: the tangram cat with a diamond head and triangle ears is a common published figure, and I drew on that memory for the head

figures.name: a sailing boat
figures.how: I worked out that the square, both small triangles and the parallelogram make a trapezoid hull, then put a large sail (the two large triangles) and a smaller jib (the medium triangle) on it; the first silhouette merged the two sails into one blob, so I moved the jib slightly off the mast to leave a gap that reads as the mast.
figures.seen_before: yes: tangram sailing boats are a standard figure; this exact arrangement I worked out myself, but the subject and the general idea are familiar

figures.name: a fish
figures.how: Two large triangles make a diamond body, and the medium triangle with the two small ones make a triangular tail; I tried the square and parallelogram as fins in three placements and kept the one with a raised dorsal fin and a small fin underneath.
figures.seen_before: unsure: fish are common tangram subjects and the diamond body with a triangle tail is an obvious form, but I do not recall this exact figure
